Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
838 PM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes to the forecast this evening other than
adjusting to current conditions and trends.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry and warm conditions expected to continue through Saturday.

- 2) Forecast remains uncertain as a coastal low tracks up the 
  Eastern Seaboard Sunday into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and warm conditions expected to continue 
through Saturday.

Surface high pressure remains overhead through Friday. This will
continue to bring very dry conditions and very light or calm 
winds. Highs will be above average with temperatures in the 60s 
to even the low 70s through Friday. Clear skies and light winds 
overnight yield favorable conditions for radiational cooling. 
Outlying areas may still drop to the upper 20s and lower 30s
tonight, although it may remain slightly warmer along the I-95
corridor where a thicker cirrus canopy will be lifting
northeastward. Lows may be a touch warmer Friday night.

While remaining overhead, surface high pressure begins shifting
northward on Saturday as a low pressure system develops off the
coast of Florida and tracks north. This results in increased
cloud cover although dry conditions and calm winds persist.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Forecast remains uncertain as a coastal low tracks 
up the Eastern Seaboard Sunday into Monday. 

An area of low pressure is forecast to develop off the Southeast 
U.S. coast late this week, then track northward along the coast this 
weekend. The low's initial forward speed is going to be slow as it 
gets trapped underneath a brief, weak upper ridge, then quickly 
picks up speed as it moves northeast with a strong upper trough 
approaching from the OH Valley. There remains considerable 
differences among the global guidance, both run to run and between 
models in each run. The ensemble guidance for both the European and 
GFS remain quite dispersive with low tracks well inland across the 
NC/VA Piedmont to well offshore of the Mid-Atlantic. 

There continues to be too much uncertainty to pin down any specific
details or impacts to our area. Rain chances Sunday into Sunday night
continue to slowly increase, especially east of the Blue Ridge with
the highest certainty east of I-95. The exact track of the low is
going to be critical to where the heaviest rain falls, though there
could be a sharp gradient on the western side of the precip shield
from heavy to very light rain amounts. It is worth mentioning 
the higher-end of the ensemble spread indicates 2-4" as a worst-
case scenario, but many members also have little to no rain for 
most of the area - this probably speak the best to how much uncertainty
remains. The location of the heaviest QPF also varies greatly from
along US-15 to the Delmarva. Continue to monitor the forecast 
over the next few days as guidance hopefully starts to converge 
on a solution for this weekend. 

A strong Canadian High builds across much of the central to eastern 
CONUS during the early part of next week. This is going to bring us 
dry, brisk, and much colder conditions. 

Models are indicating the potential for another system near Thanksgiving,
but even more spread exists with that system. More updates as we
get closer.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
VFR conditions at the terminals through at least Saturday. Light
winds out of the south to southwest this evening will be calm 
or variable overnight. On Friday, winds shift to north or 
northwesterly early, gradually becoming easterly by Saturday
while remaining around 5 knots.

We continue to monitor the developing coastal low off the coast
of Florida. As this low pressure system drifts northward, 
precipitation and sub-VFR conditions are possible by Sunday and
continuing into Monday across the terminals. The greatest 
chance will be for the eastern terminals, but there is still a
lot of uncertainty with potential storm track at this time.

&&

.MARINE...
High pressure will remain over the area tonight and Friday before
retreating to the northeast. Light winds continue to support favorable
conditions across the marine waters. A low pressure system is forecast
to develop off the coast of Florida and may bring precipitation and
increased winds to the waters on Sunday which may approach SCA criteria.
SCAs likely by late Sunday night through Monday as the low pressure
system rides up the east coast. Stronger winds will be possible,
but will depend on the exact track of the low. Should the low trend
closer to the coast, Gale-force winds can't be ruled out Monday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
High pressure will remain over the area through Friday before
moving off to the northeast Saturday into Sunday. While winds 
will remain low, RH values will remain low. Overnight 
recoveries, especially on the ridges, will be very poor as well.
Slight improvements to RH are forecast Friday and Saturday,
although afternoon values below 30 percent remain likely in
portions of the area. This dry air mass will also be paired 
with seasonably warm temperatures, so this will really act to 
dry out already very dry fuels. While fire will be slow to move 
due to lack of wind, very dry air will make for easy fire 
starts, so exercise extreme caution in the coming days. 

Not helping matters is that there is no precipitation expected 
through at least Saturday. Still watching late weekend into 
early next week for the next weather system. An area of low 
pressure developing off the southeast coast looks to move up the
east coast Sunday into Monday. Rain chances east of the Blue 
Ridge are increasing, but still not a certainty at this point. 
For areas west of the Blue Ridge, unless there is a significant 
shift, substantial rainfall seems less likely. Continue to 
monitor the latest forecast as this timeframe approaches.
